subject: Dev Essentials — Microsegment Drip + 'Quick RSVP' Link Strategy
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-12T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dev Essentials — Microsegment Drip + 'Quick RSVP' Link Strategy

Team,

Quick planning note for the inbound webinar (Dev Essentials — Low-Latency Serving patterns) launching next month. Goal here is to maximize high-quality RSVPs from engineering leads while keeping the send ops straightforward for Velocity. Key asks below — can everyone ack and update their assigned items by EOD 10/13?

1) Segments (attachment: audience_segments_v1.csv)
   - Dev Leads (primary): engineers at companies with >50 engs, product: inference/runtime tags
   - Platform Engineers (secondary): infra/platform titles, internal tooling signals
   - Neutral testers (broadcast): smaller startups for volume but single-touch cadence

2) Creative rotation / copy variants (attachment: email_copy_variants_v3.docx)
   - Variant A: Technical deep-dive (speaker + benchmark highlight)
   - Variant B: Cost/ops playbook (short bullets + ROI stat)
   - Variant C: Quick-RSVP (single-click calendar + 1-line CTA) — this is the one we need to prioritize for paid channels and partners.

3) Tracking map (attachment: tracking_map_sheet_v2.xlsx)
   - Each variant gets distinct utm_campaign + utm_content and a shortlink that drops to a Quick-RSVP anchor (no form) for ‘fast yes’.
   - For partner/prospect sends we’ll use /rsvp?token= and record in HubSpot. Please add HubSpot link ids to the map.

4) Reminder cadence / suppression windows
   - Send: Oct 28 09:00 PT primary wave
   - Reminder 1: 5 days later to non-responders (subject line variant test)
   - Final push: 24 hours before (Quick-RSVP variant only)
   - Suppression: if a contact opens within 48h of send but doesn't click, suppress additional reminders for 7 days to avoid fatigue. Ops to validate manifest before each wave.

5) Timezones and localization
   - Primary send in PT; for EU heavy segments we’ll stagger send at 09:00 CET using the same creative but local subject line iteration (Laura, you own localization).

6) Ops checklist (one-liners)
   - Marissa: finalize speaker bios + attach short 1-paragraph bios to variants.
   - Ben: populate subject-line A/B list, confirm targeting queries on CDP.
   - Laura: confirm EU send times + localization of subject line and CTA.
   - Markus (me): consolidate tracking map and hand over to CampaignOps for scheduling.

Attachments: audience_segments_v1.csv (CSV), email_copy_variants_v3.docx (DOCX), tracking_map_sheet_v2.xlsx (XLSX)

If nothing major, I’ll lock the tracking map by EOD 10/13 and hand off to CampaignOps for manifesting.

—
Markus Klein
Sr. Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks, this is clean. A couple of quick items: 

- I added concise speaker blurbs to a PDF (speaker_bios.pdf) — will attach to the technical deep-dive and Quick-RSVP variants.
- For Quick-RSVP we should keep calendar adds to Google/Outlook buttons plus a fallback single-click redirect for mobile. Ops has seen higher conversion when the CTA is literally one click.
- For the suppression note: can we make ‘‘opened but not clicked’ a separate bucket for a 72h hold instead of 48h? Gives us one more day of potential engagement.

I’ll review the segments file and flag any low-confidence emails (role/title fuzzies).

Marissa Cole
